title: Malaysia & Singapore, from the Malay and Chinese press

stories.text: Johari said the Dewan Rakyat is waiting for an explanation from Ahmad Samsuri on the status of Perikatan Nasional.
PAS and its allied parties will challenge the cancellation of Perikatan Nasional's registration in court.
Melaka state election: BN and PH will announce their candidates together this Saturday, with PN to follow next week.
The government has barred civil servants from using Waze, citing the protection of national security data.
The head of a government agency was remanded for six more days over an alleged RM30 million bribe to help companies cut RM140 million in taxes.
Electrical and electronics products make up RM1 of every RM2 of Malaysia's exports.
There is no proposal to amend Section 17 of the Federal Constitution on citizenship.
A former Temerloh district police chief was jailed eight months for accepting bribes.
The Sarawak government announced special aid worth two months' salary for its civil servants.
A teacher was injured after being attacked by a student in Kuching.
President Tharman said every country needs to be a 'bridge builder' to tackle global challenges.
PM Wong said Singapore and the UAE can step up efforts to connect businesses and investors.
Singapore's Category A COE premium passed $132,000, topping Category B for the fourth time this year.
Singapore's PSI is forecast at 101 to 160 on Thursday, and the haze may persist for the next few days.
The Hyflux trial continues after Olivia Lum and five others did not apply for a 'no case to answer' ruling.
